name: p2-2018-three-waits
title: Three places where a request can wait
spec: A left-to-right flow of four boxes joined by arrows. Box 1 'Client or router' at the left. Box 2 'Waiting queue' with the monospace metric chip 'vllm:num_requests_waiting' and the note 'The line outside a busy kitchen'. Box 3 'Running batch' with the chip 'vllm:num_requests_running' and the note 'Requests the GPU is cooking together'. Box 4 'KV cache' with the chip 'vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc'. A loop arrow from box 4 labelled 'Full: preempt the newest, recompute later' back to box 2. A side output arrow from box 3 labelled 'Tokens out: generation_tokens'. Above the chain three latency labels: 'vllm:request_queue_time_seconds: time waiting', 'vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds: TTFT', 'vllm:inter_token_latency_seconds: gap between streamed outputs'. Orange outline on the KV cache box as the place that is full before a cause is named. Bottom note: 'Name the place that is full before you name a cause.'
anchor: ### 1. Every failure is a story about three places where a request can wait
alt: A request waits in the engine's queue, runs in the batch and holds KV cache, and the metrics for each place show which one is full.
cap: A request waits in the queue, runs in the batch and holds KV cache, and each place has a vLLM metric that shows whether it is full.

name: p2-2018-queue-triage
title: Waiting high and KV low means short of replicas
spec: A decision table with three input columns and one result column, drawn as a grid. Column headings: 'Waiting queue', 'Running batch', 'KV cache usage'. Row 1 'Confirm the pattern': 'num_requests_waiting rises', 'num_requests_running at the batch limit', 'kv_cache_usage_perc below about 90 percent' with a green check on the row. A right-hand verdict box 'Short of replicas, not memory' in green. Under the table a two-branch triage: left branch 'Mitigate now: add replicas if spare GPUs, or shed load at the router' with the setting chip 'max_num_queued_reqs returns HTTP 503 at the in-flight limit'. Right branch 'Fix later: autoscale on queue depth and queue time, not GPU utilisation'. A small card 'Token throughput flat or high separates this from a hang'. Orange outline on the verdict box. Caption: 'If waiting is high and KV usage is low, you are short of replicas, not memory.'
alt: A queue growth pattern where waiting requests rise, the batch sits at its limit and KV usage stays below 90 percent, which means the fix is replicas, not memory.
cap: When waiting requests rise while KV usage stays below about 90 percent, the engine is short of replicas, not memory.

name: p2-2018-startup-or-runtime
title: Ask startup or runtime first: two OOMs, two causes
spec: A top question box 'GPU OOM: when did it die?'. It splits into two columns. Left column 'At startup': a pod restarting in a loop, a sequence of boxes 'Load weights', 'Profiling pass', 'Capture CUDA graphs', with the note 'Container exits before it listens', and mitigation chips 'gpu_memory_utilization', 'max_model_len'. Right column 'At runtime, under peak traffic': a process that dies hours later, with the causes 'Activation spike', 'Longer prompts', 'Memory fragmentation', and mitigation chips 'max_num_batched_tokens', 'cap prompt length at the gateway'. Two check boxes at the bottom: 'Read the log and kubectl describe pod, last state' and 'Check nvidia-smi for other processes'. Orange outline on the question box. Caption: 'The first points to sizing and the second points to traffic.'
anchor: ### 5. GPU OOM at startup versus at load
alt: A GPU out-of-memory failure is split by time: at startup during weight loading, profiling and CUDA graph capture, or at runtime under traffic spikes.
cap: A GPU out-of-memory failure at startup points to sizing settings, while one at runtime under peak traffic points to the traffic and prompt lengths.

name: p2-2018-quality-checks
title: Green infrastructure, unhappy users: check quality signals
spec: Left: a dashboard mock with four green status tiles labelled 'Latency fine', 'Errors low', 'GPU utilisation normal', 'Infrastructure green'. Beside it a speech bubble 'Answers are cut off, repetitive or odd'. Right: a column of four cause cards. Card 'finish_reason drift: vllm:request_success_total by finished_reason (stop, length, abort, error, repetition)'. Card 'KV-cache corruption: vllm:corrupted_requests, requests with NaNs in logits'. Card 'Speculative decoding: a small draft model proposes tokens, the main model checks them'. Card 'Quantisation: lower precision, some accuracy cost'. A fifth card at the bottom 'Sampling defaults: generation_config.json since v0.8.0'. Bottom action row: 'Stop the rollout and roll back the affected pool', 'Compare outputs on a fixed prompt set'. Orange outline on the finish_reason card. Caption: 'When infrastructure is green and users are unhappy, check finish_reason shares and the last config change.'
anchor: ### 11. Quality failures: finish_reason drift, corruption, speculative decoding and quantisation
alt: Quality failures show green infrastructure while answers are cut off, with causes such as finish reason drift, NaN corruption, speculative decoding, quantisation and sampling defaults.
cap: Quality failures leave infrastructure green, so the design checks finish_reason shares, NaN corruption counts and the last configuration change.

name: p2-2018-long-prompt-block
title: One long prefill blocks the short requests behind it
spec: Top timeline row of a shared GPU engine, left to right, with the label 'Shared batch'. Short request chips labelled 'Short chat prompt A' and 'Short chat prompt B' sit in the line behind a wide block labelled 'Long prefill from one tenant: a large compute job before the first token'. The wide block has an orange outline. Below the timeline a box 'Inter-token latency p99 rises although the queue is short and KV usage is moderate'. A bar pair in the lower left, labelled 'vllm:request_prompt_tokens': a short bar for 'p50, median prompt length' and a much longer bar for 'p99, the long tail'. A ratio callout beside the bars: 'Tail eight or more times the median is a warning sign'. Two mitigation chips on the right: 'Lower max_num_batched_tokens' and 'Route long prompts to a separate pool'. A side note: 'If tail latency rises with the prompt-length tail, isolate long prompts rather than adding replicas to the shared pool.'
alt: One tenant's long prefill blocks short requests in the shared batch, so inter-token latency rises even with a short queue and moderate KV usage.
cap: A long prefill from one tenant blocks short requests in the shared batch, so the fix is to isolate long prompts rather than add replicas.
